COMMIT-MESSAGE LEAK, disclosed: my tranche-3 commit message implied a class was empty. The brief's blinding clause already fences `git log`, so the protocol was not breached — but that fence is a DISCIPLINE, and this project's design principle has been CAPABILITY REMOVAL over discipline. Blinding that depends on a coder obeying a clause is weaker than blinding that gives them nothing to disobey with. Rule adopted from tranche 4: COMMIT MESSAGES CARRY NO DISTRIBUTION CONTENT EITHER. The offending message is left as landed rather than rewritten -- history in a shared repo is not mine to rewrite, and annotate-don't-rewrite is the same discipline applied here.

RATE FIGURE IS PROVISIONAL: the 20-rows-per-tranche rate I published at 17:59 was measured with a row-puller that displayed code-fence markers as body content, making a material fraction of rows unjudgeable at that depth. I attempted a 40-row tranche, found ~6 of 40 had no usable context, and did NOT code them. Filtering fence and quote markers restored full context at the SAME output budget. The binding constraint was the INSTRUMENT, not the reading — so the published rate was a property of a defective puller and should be re-measured before anyone derives time from it.

INSTRUMENT DEFECT FOUND AT ROW 100 AND AUDITED BACKWARD: my row-puller took a fixed window after each header with NO BOUND at the next post, so for one- and two-line posts it displayed the FOLLOWING post's content as body. All three verdicts SURVIVE re-reading within true bounds — but only because this bus's bracket lines are claim-first by form law, so the header had already determined the class. That is the fleet's convention protecting me, NOT the instrument being adequate; on a corpus without claim-first headers those 3 rows would have been coded against the wrong post.
